'''Arthur Hirsch''' (1866–1948) was a German [[mathematician]].

== Life and work ==
Hirsch completed his schooling in [[Königsberg]] in 1882 and then studied mathematics and physics in the universities of [[University of Berlin|Berlin]] and [[University of Königsberg|Königsberg]]. Among his teachers at Königsberg were [[David Hilbert]] and [[Adolf Hurwitz]].{{sfn | Eminger | 2015 | pp=113–114 }} In 1892 he received a doctorate from Königsberg for a thesis about [[linear differential equation]]s.{{sfn | Frei | Stammbach | 1992 | p=4 }}

The following year, he took his [[docent]] [[habilitation]] at [[ETH Zurich|Polytechnikum of Zurich]], where he was, successively, assistant professor from 1893, titular professor from 1897 and ordinary professor from 1903{{sfn | Eminger | 2015 | p=114 }} until his retirement in 1936.

The work of Hirsch is primarily on [[differential equation]]s and [[hypergeometric function]]s. He published seven papers about it in ''[[Mathematische Annalen]]''. Hirsch was a member of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]] from his foundation in 1910.{{sfn | Eminger | 2015 | p=115 }}
